title: Rampdown-aware load harness and tenant-aware benchmarking protocol for Dedicated
creator: Ana Morales
description: Goal: Build a reproducible load-testing harness and benchmarking methodology that captures realistic tenant mixes and rampdown behavior for Dedicated capacity. The harness must exercise autoscaler policies, burst and sustained throughput, graceful degradation (rampdown), and failure modes (node preemption/eviction). Deliverables: (1) a test harness that can run locally and in CI to produce deterministic reports; (2) a set of tenant-aware benchmark profiles (small/medium/enterprise mixes); (3) a defined customer acceptance test checklist and report template for onboarding Reserved Capacity customers. This ticket focuses on design, implementation of the harness prototype, and initial runbook and acceptance checklist creation. It intentionally differs from previous throughput suites by modelling tenant-level QoS isolation, cache-warmup effects across tenants, and autoscaler rampdown hysteresis under sustained overload.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can generate multi-tenant traffic patterns with configurable tenant counts (1..500) and QPS distributions
Reports include p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, tail-latency per-tenant, and observed scheduler queue lengths
Autoscaler policy permutations (conservative, balanced, aggressive) are testable and saved as named runs
Rampdown scenarios (scale-down under 10 minutes and 30 minutes) reproduce within 10% across repeated runs
Run outputs produce a customer-facing acceptance report and a machine-readable artifact (CSV/JSON) that can be uploaded to Console
Integration tests validate harness against the staging Dedicated fleet with synthetic node preemption and simulated KV-cache cold starts
Solutions Engineering signs off on the onboarding checklist and the first customer acceptance run passes for an internal partner
tasks: Design load profile spec: tenant weight distributions, prompt length distributions, KV cache hit/warm ratios
Implement traffic generator worker (Go) with tenant sharding and per-tenant token counters
Add scheduler metrics hooks: queue depth, per-model active requests, kernel-selection breakdown
Implement autoscaler driver to swap policy configs and observe scaling events during runs
Build rampdown scenarios: graceful (scale-down with draining) and abrupt (preempt and note tail spikes)
Write run orchestration CLI and GitHub Actions workflow for nightly benchmark runs
Author customer acceptance checklist and report template in Confluence and link to onboarding playbook

2025-03-01: Infra quota approved; started first staging run with conservative autoscaler policy. Early results show unexpected p99 spikes during scale-down, capturing evidence for scheduler adjustment.

notes: Key design decisions: use tenant-sharded generators to model correlated bursts, include KV-cache cold start during scale-up, and add a 'maintenance' perturbation (10% of nodes artificially delayed) to validate graceful degradation. Benchmark naming convention: <mix>-<autoscaler>-<ramp>-<timestamp>. Example: enterprise-balanced-10m-20250301. Execution considerations: reproducibility requires seeding RNGs and version-locking model binaries and kernel tables.
